components.name: marginal_outcomes
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Same-population A0 reconstruction. Lognormal weight; beta-distributed PFS on [1,5] rounded to 1/15; negative-binomial integer gng on [0,512]; beta dd100 and dd1000 on [0,1]. Distributional shapes are assumptions. Beta and negative-binomial parameters match source population-style moments; randomized finite cohorts need not match exactly. Weight is truncated at 180 kg only at baseline. Truncation and PFS rounding slightly alter fitted moments.

components.name: conditional_quantile_sampling
components.source_to_target_assumptions: At each observed visit/outcome margin, sample one uniform value per equal-probability stratum and assign quantiles by stochastic Gaussian latent ranks. This produces stochastic cohorts conditional on supplied marginals with less finite-cohort marginal variability than iid sampling. It does not reproduce individual rows and does not provide a sampling-uncertainty model.

components.name: longitudinal_and_cross_endpoint_dependence
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Working latent persistent variance fractions are weight 0.85, pfs 0.60, gng 0.45, dd100 0.60, dd1000 0.60. Gaussian random intercept plus independent visit innovations, followed by within-observed-margin rank transformation, gives persistent subject rankings. These numbers are unestimated modeling choices and are not exact observed-scale ICCs. Outcome processes are independent across endpoints as a parsimonious unidentified-dependence closure; this is an imposed assumption, not evidence that any true correlation or weight association is zero.

components.name: missingness
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Exact visit/outcome observed counts at n=75; int(round(n_observed*n/75)) at other n. Rank availability scores composed of independent normal person (variance 0.50), shared person-visit (0.30), and endpoint-visit (0.20) components. The overlap and persistent absence are assumed; no monotone dropout is enforced. Scores are independent of all outcome latent variables, giving a conditional-count MCAR mechanism. Source individual masks and informative missingness are unknown.

components.name: synthetic_identity
components.source_to_target_assumptions: New numeric person IDs 1 through n; every person has one row at each declared visit. Local default_rng(seed), no file or network I/O, and no evidence mutation.

scenarios.assumption: One selected working reconstruction with assumed positive within-endpoint persistence, independent cross-endpoint processes, and outcome-independent shared missingness propensity. Resource allocation of 20 cohorts is not a posterior probability.
scenarios.inclusion_rationale: The packet identifies marginal scales, counts, eligibility, and measurement support. This one transparent conventional distribution/correlation construction provides reproducible rehearsal cohorts without attempting to recover reserved analyses.
scenarios.scientific_scenario_differences: Only one scenario is committed; no alternative scientific scenarios were examined.
unresolved_dependencies: Cross-endpoint covariance, including between discounting conditions, remains unidentified; independence is assumed.
Within-person lag covariance and random slope/change covariance are unprovided; fixed latent persistence is assumed.
Missing-mask overlap and outcome-dependent attrition are unprovided; correlated MCAR masks are assumed.
Distribution shape, boundary masses, PFS item completeness, and individual measurement error are unprovided.
